subject: resolution of the 1.469761 vs 1469.8 ms discrepancy (docs/status.md section 3.3)
based_on: per-run originals fetched from the load host (ramona-vm-q) and verified here; nothing in historical evidence was rewritten
finding: The archived narrative's 'p99 1,469.8 ms' was a UNIT MISREADING of the per-run summary value 1.469761, which the summary.json reports in milliseconds within latency_ms.

thingsboard-n1-r200-20261027T233211Z summary.json: target_rate 200, steady_duration_s 60, requests 12001, achieved_rate 200.017, error_rate 1.0 (steady-phase error rate 100.000%), latency_ms {min 0.405045, med 0.736945, p95 0.997103, p99 1.469761, max 18.666156}.

The p99 1.469761 ms is therefore the sub-millisecond latency profile of FAILING requests on that run (all steady-phase requests errored; every latency is one instant connection failure), not a 1.47 s service latency. The combined all-summaries.txt row is this same millisecond profile.

Consequential: the archived 'p99 1.47 s, variability is real' statement and the VU-sizing lesson derived from confirm-run latency are WITHDRAWN in this scope; the valid TB 200 r/s confirm-run latency statements remain those from the other runs (first pass p95 ~230 ms; the r232557/r232253 per-run files are now available for the authoritative quote).
impact: docs/status.md section 3.3 is closed as a unit-misreading; no latency above 50 r/s is quoted from the erroneous sources. The correct confirm-run latency figures at 200 r/s must be read from the fetched per-run originals (per-run-originals/results/thingsboard-n1-r200-20261027T232557Z/summary.json).
